question: How loud is Liverpool Street to Bethnal Green by TfL's own measurement, and what do our phone measurements add?
norm_question: how loud is liverpool street to bethnal green by tfls own measurement and what do our phone measurements add

answer.text: TfL recorded 87 dB LAeq eastbound and 86 dB LAeq westbound in-cab on 24 June 2024, while our saloon phone data add a 0.54 dB within-trip contrast and indicative whole-trip levels of 91.9 and 87.3 dB(A).

verified_claims.text: In TfL's own measurements from within the train operator's cab on 24 June 2024 (FOI-1231-2425), Liverpool Street to Bethnal Green recorded 87 dB LAeq eastbound and Bethnal Green to Liverpool Street recorded 86 dB LAeq westbound.

citations.quote:
Please see below the noise levels recorded on the Monday 24
June 2024, these measurements were taken from within the train operator's cab.

verified_claims.text: A secondary press report by Brixton Buzz (via JRPass) cites a higher figure of 92.8 decibels for Liverpool Street to Bethnal Green, which is not TfL's primary 24 June 2024 cab measurement.

citations.quote: Liverpool Street to Bethnal Green (Central line) – 92.8 decibels

verified_claims.text: Our uncalibrated relative phone-audio recordings in the passenger saloon measure -18.66 dBFS(A) eastbound (n=6) and -18.8 dBFS(A) westbound (n=5) between Liverpool Street and Bethnal Green, adding a mean within-trip contrast of 0.54 dB above Bethnal Green to Mile End across 10 of 11 trips (a NO-GO verdict as the difference is below 1 dB).

Our phone sound level meter app adds indicative whole-trip passenger-saloon levels between Liverpool Street and Mile End (including platform and dwell time) of 91.9 dB(A) LAeq eastbound (n=1) and 87.3 dB(A) LAeq westbound (n=1), though the app is validated only up to about 85 dB(A) so these indicative readings may read low and are not like-for-like with TfL's per-section in-cab figures.
